beats.care: Depend on public toilets while commuting? BMC says it will track them digitally through its ToiletSeva app.
beats.what: QCI, hired by BMC, checked 837 of 896 pay-and-use toilets: 8 got A, 566 B, 90 C and 173 D.
beats.why: BMC wants the grades to push repairs and a standard design and upkeep plan for public toilets.

cards.body: That's under 1% of the 837 toilets checked so far.
cards.caption: toilets that got Grade A

cards.body: BMC's draft pay-and-use policy proposes Rs 5 for women's urinals, up from Rs 2, a new Rs 1 fee for men's urinals, and Rs 10 for bathing. It isn't final.
cards.title: Fees may rise too

cards.body: Activist Vinod Gholap called the result "a wake-up call for the BMC."

opts: The lowest-scoring toilets, needing big fixes
cards.q: What does a Grade D mean in this survey?
cards.why: D was the lowest grade, for toilets that scored worst across the five checks.

hook: How many of Mumbai's public toilets *got a top grade*?

learn.t: Each toilet was scored out of 100 on five areas, including access for children and people with disabilities.

sources.name: Free Press Journal
sources.title: Mumbai: BMC Assessment Finds 173 Of 837 Pay-And-Use Toilets Graded D, Only 8 Secure Top Grade A

tldr: A Quality Council of India check graded only 8 of 837 BMC pay-and-use toilets 'A', while 173 got the lowest 'D' grade.
watch: Toilet operators in North Mumbai served BMC notices have three months to renovate.
